label: update gate higher when agent leans/chooses a2, lower for a1 and after a1 S2 unrewarded
terms: np.tanh(choice) ;; np.tanh(choice)*np.exp((ep_trial-99)/6.0) ;; (prev_action == 2) ;; last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; np.exp((ep_trial-99)/6.0) ;; (ep_trial % 10)*(ep_dec>=7) ;; (phase==D2)*(action==2)
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 2 is dominated by timing (sits near 0.9 and collapses over the last ~20 trials of the episode; timing R^2 0.84). Beyond timing, its magnitude mainly tracks the agent choice side: it is higher when the policy favours a2 (graded -tanh(policy logit a1-a2), all phases, stronger late in episode), higher after a previous a2 choice, and higher at D2 when a2 was just chosen; it is lowest after an a1 -> S2 unrewarded trial (about -0.06, strongest at GO/D2). Reward and value contribute little (value decile R^2 0.02; this-trial reward 0.00). Part of the gain comes from fine within-decile timing late in the episode (exp((ep_trial-99)/6) and trial-within-decile terms), which the per-decile baseline misses. A future-choice version ((action==2) instead of the policy logit) scored dev 0.518 vs 0.50 for this observed/model-only version; recorded the observed one. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.498 vs all-cue ceiling 0.60 (83%).

issues: The test score reproduces: 0.498 beyond timing (timing-only R^2 0.839). The behavioural claims hold. Residual tables: a1 S2 u is lowest at GO (-0.139) and D2 (-0.12). At D1 it is only level with a1 S1 u (-0.078 vs -0.077), so the claim 'strongest at GO and D2' is correct. Prev a2 is positive and prev a1 negative. Value deciles are flat (ref 0.02) and this trial's reward is 0.00.

The late-episode growth of the choice effect is real, but its shape is wrong. tanh(choice)*exp((ep_trial-99)/6) gets almost no weight (-0.008). Adding tanh(choice)*ep_trial/100 raises test to 0.542. Replacing the /6 interaction with tanh(choice)*exp((ep_trial-99)/20) gives 0.522 on its own. So the choice effect builds up slowly over the second half of the episode, not just in the last ~6 trials.

A large part of the 'beyond timing' score is just finer timing that the per-decile baseline misses. The three timing-shape terms alone (exp/6, exp/20, ep_trial%10 late) score 0.131 on test. Adding exp((ep_trial-99)/20) to the original 7 terms jumps test from 0.498 to 0.590 (dev 0.581). The 'all-cue ceiling 0.60 (83%)' comparison is therefore misleading: that ceiling uses decile timing only, and the behavioural content beyond fine timing is about 0.40-0.46.

Ablations: tanh(choice) alone scores 0.379. Choice + prev_action + a1S2u + D2*a2, with no timing terms, scores 0.436. Removing last_is('a1 S2 u') drops test to 0.469. Each named behavioural term contributes.

Misses on the original and the improved terms leave only moderate structured errors (|error| <= 0.04). Under-prediction: GO after a1 S1 r +0.04, D1 after a1 S2 u +0.035 (a1S2u is overstated at D1). Over-prediction: GO after a2 S2 u -0.038, D2 after a1 S1 r / a1 S2 r about -0.03. The worst windows are late-episode (t87-95) episodes where z stays far above the predicted timing decline (e.g. 0.7 vs 0.38) during a2 runs. That is mostly between-episode variation in timing that no term fixes. No large systematic class remains.

Minor: at D1 the policy-decile residual is not monotonic (deciles 3-4 highest, +0.067), so a single graded tanh(choice) across all phases is approximate. The D2*(action==2) term is observed at D2 (equivalent to in_action==2), so no future-variable issue arises. The improved set below uses in_action.
skeptic.revised_label: update gate higher when the policy leans a2 (effect builds over the second half of the episode), after a previous a2 choice and at D2 after choosing a2; lowest after a1 S2 unrewarded (GO/D2); plus finer late-episode timing
